preamble: The voiced aspirated velar stop [ɡʱ] loses its oral closure and only the breathy component survives as [h]. In Italic, PIE *gʰ (merged with *ǵʰ) gave Latin h through a fricative stage reconstructed as Proto-Italic *χ (hostis, hiems). Other branches keep a stop (Greek kʰ, Germanic and Slavic g); the Middle Indo-Aryan reduction of gh to voiced [ɦ] is filed under g_aspirated > ɦ.

examples.note: 'stranger, enemy'; via Proto-Italic *hostis (*χ); cognate with Proto-Germanic *gastiz (English guest)
'winter'; Latin merges palatovelar *ǵʰ with plain *gʰ as h
